svg.data-vd-play-label: Play: how a lake loses its oxygen
svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "A healthy lake next to farmland: plants photosynthesise and the water has plenty of dissolved oxygen."], [1.5, "1. Rain washes nitrate and phosphate fertiliser from the fields into the lake (run-off and leaching)."], [4, "2. The extra nutrients cause an algal bloom on the surface."], [6.5, "3. The algae block the light: plants under the water cannot photosynthesise and die."], [9, "4. Bacteria decompose the dead plants and algae. They multiply and use up the dissolved oxygen in respiration."], [12, "5. Fish and other animals die from lack of oxygen. Biodiversity falls."]]
svg.title: Eutrophication
svg.desc: A lake beside farmland: fertiliser run-off, algal bloom, light blocked, plants die, decomposers use up oxygen, fish die; an oxygen meter falls and a flow chart builds.
svg.text: The sequence of events after fertiliser enters a lake.

g.data-info: Nitrate and phosphate fertilisers (or sewage) are washed into rivers and lakes by rain: leaching and run-off.
Extra nutrients make algae grow very fast, covering the surface.
Algae at the surface stop light reaching plants under the water, so they cannot photosynthesise and die.
Bacteria decompose the dead plants and algae. They respire aerobically and use up the dissolved oxygen (high biochemical oxygen demand, BOD).

g.text: bacteria decompose dead material and use up O₂

g.data-info: Not enough dissolved oxygen for aerobic respiration.
